Hi Samira / Alan — thanks again for the call earlier. Per our discussion I attached a first-pass MAP worksheet and sketched the milestone for Data Handling & Compliance that we should land before procurement signs the SOW. I want to capture the responsibilities, target close date, and dependencies so we can present a clean timeline to your legal and security teams.

High-level summary (please confirm or correct):
- Milestone: Data retention, audit logging, and PHI/PII handling policy alignment
- Target close date: 2027-03-31 (aligns with procurement window for Q2 go-live)
- Redwood responsibilities: provide retention configuration options, audit-log export format, SOC 2 artifact list, and technical architecture note for PHI isolation
- Skyline responsibilities: confirm retention policy (retention period by data class), identify data steward(s), complete security questionnaire, and provide list of systems that will integrate with Redwood (EHR, analytics)
- Dependencies: legal review of DPA addendum, SOC 2 evidence upload (Redwood deliverable), and network/VPC peering date

Specific asks from your side (actionable next steps):
1) Please confirm the desired retention windows for the following classes (example values below):
   - Audit logs (API calls & token-level events): 7 years (requested by compliance)
   - Conversation transcripts (de-identified): 3 years
   - PHI/PII raw artifacts: 7 years, encrypted at rest, restricted access
2) Identify the person who will own the MAP milestone on your side (name + email).
3) Share any mandatory regulatory constraints (state statutes or payer contracts) that require specific retention or reporting cadence.

Technical notes included in the attachment: audit log schema, sample retention toggles in the console, and recommended S3 export cadence. If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute technical review with our security engineer to walk the SOC 2 artifacts and the S3 export pipeline.

Planned internal follow-up: Marissa will prepare an updated SOW sketch once these retention windows are confirmed; Laura will coordinate legal engagement.

Thanks — looking forward to your confirmations so we can lock the MAP milestone.

—

Thanks Aditya — good recap and thank you for the attachment. Quick clarifications from our end: we reviewed with privacy and they flagged a couple of non-negotiables.

Quoted from their note: "Skyline Health requires: (A) Audit logs for all API activity and user-level access records retained for at least 7 years; (B) PHI artifacts must be retained per state health record requirements (typically 7 years adult, longer for minors) and must be cryptographically segregated from non-PHI data; (C) A documented chain-of-custody for exports and an immutable audit trail for any data access or deletion requests."

Practical asks:
- Can Redwood provide an immutable export of audit logs (append-only) and a tamper-evident checksum for each export?
- Does your current private deployment (VPC) support customer-managed KMS and HSM integration? We need us to bring our own KMS for encryption key ownership.
- For PHI workflows, we need clearly documented escalation times (>24h SLA for access requests) — can you capture that as part of the MAP?

We will nominate an internal owner by EOD Thursday. For now, please treat procurement@skylinehealth.com as procurement contact (they will start the SOW review).

Forwarding your original message below for context.

Samira — thanks for the fast turnaround and for outlining the compliance constraints. Short answers below and next steps: 

1) Immutable audit exports + checksum: Yes — our export pipeline supports append-only S3 exports with SHA-256 checksums and manifest files; we will include checksum verification steps in the MAP deliverable. I attached the DPO QA doc that shows the export format and sample manifest.
2) Customer-managed keys (BYOK): Yes for Private deployments — we support customer-managed KMS, including integration guidance for AWS KMS and HSM-backed keys. For Hosted accounts we offer a managed KMS but can discuss an enterprise option for key isolation if needed.
3) Escalation and access SLA: We can commit to documenting an access-request escalation timeline inside the MAP. Proposed Redwood commitment: initial acknowledgement within 8 business hours, technical response within 24 business hours, and a full remediation/closure plan to be agreed in SOW.

Updated MAP link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-example-map (I've updated the milestone row to include the export manifest, BYOK note, and proposed SLAs).

Next steps:
- Samira / procurement: confirm the data steward name so we can assign responsibility in the MAP (requested EOD Thu).
- Redwood: Marissa will circulate an updated SOW sketch by Monday 2027-02-14; Laura will compile SOC 2 artifacts and place them in the secure share.
- Book technical review: I'll propose times for a 30-min security deep-dive (security eng + solutions arch) — proposed window Fri 2027-02-12 09:30-11:30 PT.

If that works I'll schedule and include calendar invites.

Thanks — we'll keep this thread as the canonical MAP milestone conversation and version control the attached worksheet.

Best,
